decisions.reason: The firm has just invested in tooling and finishes for this new lever family, which is core to its announced coordinated-family strategy, and a one-year-old product is far too new to judge, so it will persist.

The mitred lever family fits the firm's architecture-aware design positioning and has sunk design and tooling costs, so modest visibility would be blamed on the short time since launch rather than taken as a reason to drop it.
A multifunctional lever supports the barrier-free, one-stop system direction the firm has publicly committed to, which makes management unlikely to withdraw it after only one year.
Although it is only briefly mentioned, this single lever represents recent investment within the firm's core handle range, and early weak signals would be attributed to normal ramp-up time.
The collection has its own page, a public launch and a German Design Award, a highly visible commitment that management will defend and continue.
The patinated bronze finish draws on the firm's proprietary finishing know-how and its sustainable-materials story, and keeping a finish option costs little, so it will be retained.
